title: An elementary obstruction to same-ground-set matroid-rank approximation

initial.phase: root read full controlling TeX before consulting cited proof bodies; archived variants were listed by path and hash alone
initial.scope: No dimension-independent two-sided factor for normalized nonnegative monotone submodular functions approximated by an ordinary unscaled matroid rank on the same finite ground set.
initial.proof: Every singleton positive excludes loops, giving R integer 1..n and alpha>=1. A basis and full-set tests for sqrt force alpha>=sqrt R and sqrt n/R, and uniform U_R,n attains their max at each R. Exact min and at cubes follow. For rational g on m² ground-set, the basis gives m <= alpha+alpha(m-1)/R, full set gives R>=m/alpha; then alpha²+alpha>=m. Concave increments proof is correct at arbitrary subset overlaps. Terminal discrete slopes give the uniform-sum representation and lifted copies give exact rational representation on block unions.
initial.boundary: Does not claim general minimax exponent, scaled or weighted ranks, rank sums, expanded ground set, or a query lower bound. Exact historical source's per-dimension quantifier inferred as conventional and clearly marked.

math: Normalized singleton values rule out loops, so rank R is positive. A basis and the full ground set force α≥sqrt(R), α≥sqrt(n)/R respectively, hence α≥n^(1/6). The fixed-rank optimum is attained by the uniform matroid, with cube equality after minimizing over R. The rational family has cardinality slopes 1 then 1/m, is a convex combination of rank-one and free rank, and puts R≥m/α in the basis bound m≤α+α(m−1)/R, giving α²+α≥m. Empty ground and minimal ranks are correct. Positive scaling can beat the ordinary sixth-root estimate already at n=16; no scaled theorem is claimed.
